title: Formation of a Protostellar Multiple System via Rotational Fragmentation
question: Determine the dominant formation mechanism of the compact protostellar multiple system in the dense core G205.46-14.56-N2 and its host filament G205.46-14.56.

data.sensitivity: ~0.1 mJy beam^-1 (combined all), ~0.35 mJy beam^-1 (ACA+TM2), ~2 mJy beam^-1 (ACA alone)

what.value: Dust temperature and column density maps derived from Herschel data

evidence.quote: We also used the dust temperature and column density maps derived from Herschel data

what.value: Linewidth ΔV = 0.9 km s^-1 from NRO 45-m observations of the N2H+ J=1-0 line

evidence.loc: B. VIRIAL ANALYSIS OF THE DENSE MOLECULAR CORE
evidence.quote: We adopt p = 2, ∆V = 0.9 km s−1 from NRO 45-m observations of the N2H+ J=1-0 line (Kim et al. 2020), and R = 7000 au as derived from JCMT data.

what.value: Total stellar mass of the core of approximately 6.3 M_sun

evidence.loc: B. VIRIAL ANALYSIS OF THE DENSE MOLECULAR CORE
evidence.quote: The total stellar mass estimated by Reipurth et al. (2023) is approximately 6.3 M⊙.

what.value: Ratio of rotational energy to gravitational energy of the filament G205.46-14.56 (beta ~ 0.04)

evidence.quote: Finally, the dense filament G205.46-14.56, which hosts this core, is also rotating with β ∼0.04 (Hsieh et al. 2021).

recipe.goal: Extract dense structures across multi-scale continuum maps and measure their sizes and masses
recipe.method: Run Astrodendro on Herschel 500 um, JCMT 850 um, ACA 1.3 mm, and combined ALMA 1.3 mm images to identify leaves; for elongated structures with axis ratio > 2 (ACA 1.3 mm main structure), fit three 2D Gaussians in CASA imfit using Spitzer 4.5 um as a reference; compute beam-deconvolved effective radii and optically thin dust masses.
key_parameters: min_value = 5 sigma, min_delta = 1 sigma, min_npix = 1 synthesized beam, major-to-minor axis ratio < 2
assumptions: Optically thin dust continuum emission; gas-to-dust ratio R_gd = 100; dust opacity kappa_nu = 0.9, 1.5, and 3.9 cm^2 g^-1 for 1.3 mm, 850 um, and 500 um; dust temperatures from Herschel (13-16 K); mean molecular weight mu = 2.37; distance D = 404 pc

recipe.goal: Analyze hierarchical fragmentation separations and compare with thermal Jeans lengths
recipe.method: Construct a minimum spanning tree (MST) for identified structures at each scale to measure projected nearest-neighbor separations, and calculate thermal Jeans lengths of the parental structures.
assumptions: Homogeneous spherical mass density derived from M and R_eff-de; for core N2 Jeans length, total mass is 8.6 M_sun including gas and stellar mass

recipe.goal: Evaluate gravitational binding of the dense core G205.46-14.56-N2 via virial analysis
recipe.method: Calculate virial mass M_vir for a power-law density distribution and compare with combined gas and stellar mass of the core.
key_parameters: R = 7000 au, Delta V = 0.9 km s^-1
assumptions: Power-law density index p = 2, non-spherical shape correction a_2 ~ 1 (aspect ratio < 2), stellar mass = 6.3 M_sun from Reipurth et al. (2023)

recipe.goal: Identify protostellar outflows and derive outflow dynamical properties and accretion rates
recipe.method: Visually identify outflows in high-velocity CO J=2-1 integrated intensity maps (blueshifted -15 to 5 km s^-1, redshifted 15 to 35 km s^-1), and calculate outflow gas mass, dynamical timescale, mass-loss rate, outflow force, and protostellar mass accretion rate.
key_parameters: Velocity integration ranges: -15 to 5 km s^-1 (blueshifted) and 15 to 35 km s^-1 (redshifted)
assumptions: Typical jet/wind velocity V_w ~ 150 km s^-1; ratio of wind mass-loss rate to mass accretion rate M_dot_w / M_dot_acc ~ 0.1; entrainment efficiency f_ent = 0.25

recipe.goal: Measure core velocity gradients and rotational-to-gravitational energy ratios across spatial scales
recipe.method: Stack three H2CO J=3-2 line transitions, generate moment 1 maps for ACA, ACA+TM2, and ACA+TM1+TM2 datasets, extract position-velocity cuts, perform linear fits to measure velocity gradients, and compute rotational-to-gravitational energy ratio beta sin^2(i).
assumptions: r^-2 density profile with p/q = 0.22 (also compared with uniform density profile which increases beta by a factor of three)

recipe.goal: Measure large-scale cloud velocity gradient around the filament
recipe.method: Grid PMO 13CO (1-0) OTF data into 3D cubes using GILDAS, construct moment 1 map over 6-14 km s^-1, and fit a linear velocity gradient along a cut across the filament.
key_parameters: Velocity range 6-14 km s^-1; Blueshifted 6 to 9.5 km s^-1; Redshifted 10.5 to 14 km s^-1; grid spacing 30''

score_reason: The paper provides clear analytical formulas and Astrodendro parameters, and the ALMA data are public under 2018.1.00302.S, but calibration/imaging details are deferred to Dutta et al. (2020) and key outflow calculation parameters (T_ex, tau_12, integration regions) and PV cut coordinates are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project 2018.1.00302.S is public in the archive, the core physical results (continuum fluxes, masses, MST separations, H2CO velocity gradients, and outflow properties) are quantitative, and the Astrodendro/kinematic analysis recipe is straightforward to re-implement once the ALMASOP imaging setup from Dutta et al. (2020) is consulted.
